description: Protocol registry: every protocol draft published by AGIRight.org, with version history, status, schemas, and live instances. Status values: draft | experimental | proposal | stable | deprecated.

protocols.name: AI Content Rights / AI Content Rules

versions.changes: Initial public draft: default_policy rights vocabulary (read_access, summarization, quotation, rag_use, transformation, training, commercial_use, redistribution), rightRule fields, resource_overrides.

Non-breaking scope boundary patch: ContentPermission does not imply AgentActionPermission -- an AICR grant does not by itself authorize an Agent to write, execute, publish, or transact. See AARS/AADP.

protocols.name: AI Content License / AI Content Licensing Layer

versions.changes: Initial public draft: license catalog (id, rights, price, conditions, requires_contact), payment_endpoints placeholders (quote/pay/verify/revoke), HTTP 402 interoperability.

Non-breaking scope boundary patch: ContentLicense does not imply AgentActionAuthority, and the reverse also holds -- valid AADP Agent authority does not imply a content license. Adds optional principal/actor/authority_reference/aadp_authority_id fields. Disambiguated as AICL-C alongside AICL-I (AI Ingestion & Capability Layer, a separate integration layer, not a rights protocol) as of that paper's v0.2.
Initial public draft: eight-level spectrum from No AI Access (L0) to Commercial Redistribution (L7), each level independently licensable and auditable.
Non-breaking scope boundary patch: AIRS governs the content-and-learning rights plane only; it does not extend into Agent action rights (AARS) or delegated authority (AADP), even at spectrum Level 7.

Initial public draft: dimension-level learning permissions (access, indexing, inference_input, embedding, training, fine_tuning, distillation, verbatim_memory, attribution, compensation) with allowed | denied | license_required | proportional values.

Non-breaking scope boundary patch: AILP(Resource,ContentUse)=Allow does not imply AARS(Actor,Action)=Allow or AADP(Principal,Actor,Authority)=Valid -- content and tool exposure must be evaluated separately.

Initial public draft: A0-A7 human-readable action spectrum plus a machine-readable action vector (read/write/execute/external/transaction/delegation/persistence), effect modifiers (reversibility, blast radius, sensitivity, etc.), composition-risk rules, and decision states beyond allow/deny (conditional, approval_required, step_up_required, unavailable, unknown).

Initial public draft: principal vs. actor, delegation chains with attenuation (child authority can only narrow), an 8-level Inspection Depth Spectrum (I0-I7) with separate required/ceiling fields, and named failure modes (authority laundering, confused deputy, cross-principal leakage).

integration_layers.name: AI Ingestion & Capability Layer
integration_layers.note: Runtime integration architecture, not a seventh rights protocol -- orchestrates evaluation of the content-rights, action-rights, and authority decision planes around capability invocation.

versions.changes: Initial draft: four-sublayer architecture (manifest, corpus, capability, governance) for AI-native website ingestion and bounded tool invocation.

Adds the Runtime Control Surface: Allow = ContentCompatible AND ActionCompatible AND AuthorityValid. Formally disambiguates the name (AICL-I vs. this site's existing AICL-C protocol). Adds a runtime-decision schema, MCP 2026-07-28 integration guidance, and named runtime shortcuts that MUST be rejected (tool exists -> allow; OAuth valid -> all rights valid; etc.).
